title: No Internet Connection
cardText: Diagnose devices that cannot access websites, online services, or cloud applications.
Determine whether the problem is Wi-Fi, Ethernet, DNS, router, ISP, VPN, or device related.
Troubleshoot fibre and 4G/5G mobile broadband connections.
text: This guide is for devices that cannot access the internet.
Determine whether the problem affects one device or multiple devices.
Test a computer using a phone hotspot when appropriate.
For network-wide problems, identify whether the service uses fibre, mobile broadband or another connection type.
Check local connectivity before resetting equipment or changing router settings.
Contact the internet provider when local troubleshooting does not restore service.

checkAffectedDevices.title: Check whether other devices have internet access
body: Test another phone, tablet, laptop or computer on the same network.
On a phone, temporarily disable mobile data to ensure you are testing its Wi-Fi connection.
This determines whether the issue is isolated to one device or affects the entire network.
If only one device is affected, continue with device troubleshooting.
If multiple devices cannot access the internet, investigate the router and internet service.

link.name: Internet connection test
link.description: A simple external website to check whether internet access is working. It will not load while the connection is offline.

testPhoneHotspot.title: Test the computer using a phone hotspot
body: On a phone with working mobile data, enable Personal Hotspot or Mobile Hotspot.
Disconnect the affected computer from its normal Wi-Fi network and connect it to the phone hotspot.
Try opening several websites.
If internet access works through the hotspot, investigate the computer's connection to its normal network.
If it still fails, investigate the computer's network configuration. A failed hotspot test alone does not prove the computer is faulty.
Turn off the hotspot after testing to avoid unnecessary mobile data usage.
If a hotspot is unavailable, continue with the normal connection checks.

checkConnectionType.title: Identify the computer's connection type
body: Determine whether the affected computer normally connects using Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
If you tested a phone hotspot, disconnect it and return to the normal network.
Select the connection type used by the affected computer.

checkWifiConnection.title: Check Wi-Fi connection status
body: Verify the device is connected to the correct wireless network.
Check whether Windows reports Connected, Connected without Internet or Disconnected.
Reconnect to the correct network if necessary.

reconnectWifi.title: Reconnect to Wi-Fi
body: Connect to the correct wireless network.
Verify the Wi-Fi password is correct.
Once connected, test internet access again.
If the problem persists, continue troubleshooting the network connection.

checkEthernetCable.title: Check Ethernet cable
body: Ensure the Ethernet cable is firmly connected at both ends.
Look for link lights on the network port if available.
Try another cable or port if possible.

replaceEthernetCable.title: Replace Ethernet cable
body: A damaged or disconnected Ethernet cable can prevent network connectivity.
Replace the cable and retest the connection.

testWebsiteAccess.title: Test access to websites
body: Open a web browser and try several different websites.
Do not rely on a single website because that site itself may be offline.
Check whether some websites work or whether all websites fail.

dnsIssueCheck.title: Check for DNS issues
body: If some websites work but others do not, DNS resolution may be failing.
DNS translates website names into IP addresses.
Compare results from several websites or services.
A DNS problem can make the internet appear partially broken.

changeDnsServer.title: Change DNS server
body: Try a reliable public DNS provider such as Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Google DNS (8.8.8.8), if appropriate.
Flush the DNS cache if necessary.
Retest website access after making changes.
On managed networks, check with the administrator before changing DNS settings.

checkNetworkAdapter.title: Check network adapter status
body: Open network settings and confirm the network adapter is enabled.
Disable and re-enable the adapter if necessary.
A disabled adapter can prevent internet access even when the hardware appears normal.

enableAdapter.title: Enable network adapter
body: Enable the disabled network adapter.
Reconnect to the network and test internet access.

checkIpAddress.title: Check IP address assignment
body: Open Command Prompt and run ipconfig.
Check that the network adapter has a valid IP address and default gateway.
An address beginning with 169.254 may indicate that Windows failed to obtain an address from DHCP.
Check whether the device uses a deliberately configured static address before changing anything.

renewIpAddress.title: Renew IP address
body: Disconnect and reconnect to the network.
Restart the device or renew its DHCP lease.
On Windows, ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew can request another IPv4 address when DHCP is in use.
If the problem persists, investigate router DHCP settings.
Do not remove a required static IP configuration.

checkVpnUsage.title: Check for VPN usage
body: Determine whether a VPN is active.
A misconfigured or disconnected VPN can block internet access.
Temporarily disconnect the VPN if permitted.

disableVpn.title: Disable VPN temporarily
body: Disconnect the VPN temporarily if authorised.
Test websites and online services again.
If internet access returns, review the VPN configuration.

restartDevice.title: Restart the device
body: Restart the affected computer or device.
Temporary networking problems can sometimes be resolved by a reboot.
Retest internet access after startup.

resetNetworkSettings.title: Reset network settings
body: Consider resetting network settings after simpler troubleshooting has failed.
A network reset can remove saved Wi-Fi networks, VPN configuration and other custom settings.
Record important configuration details before proceeding.
Reconnect to the network and retest internet access.

deviceNetworkEscalation.title: Further device diagnostics required
body: The problem appears isolated to this device.
Investigate network drivers, operating system settings, security software and hardware faults.
Review the results of the phone hotspot test if one was performed.
Escalate if the device still cannot connect.

checkRouterStatus.title: Check router and modem status lights
body: Inspect the router or modem for warning lights and missing internet indicators.
If you have a separate fibre ONT, inspect its lights as well.
A router using mobile broadband may have separate 4G/5G signal and network indicators.
Compare the lights with the equipment's documentation because their meanings vary by model.
Record any red warning lights or connection errors.

link.name: Chorus ONT-500 guide
link.description: Official example of fibre ONT status lights and equipment connections.

checkRouterStatus.caption: Example Chorus fibre ONT indicators. Other ONTs and mobile broadband routers have different lights.

restartRouter.title: Restart the router or modem
body: Switch off the router or modem and wait at least 30 seconds.
Turn it back on and allow several minutes for the connection to establish.
If you use fibre with a separate ONT, leave the ONT powered on during this initial router-only restart.
If you use mobile broadband, allow time for the router to register with the cellular network.
Test internet access again.

checkIspOutage.title: Check ISP outage information
body: Use another working internet connection or mobile data to check your ISP's outage information.
Look for known fibre, fixed-line or mobile network problems in your area.
If the provider reports an outage, further local changes may not help.
If no outage is reported, continue investigating.

waitForIspRepair.title: Wait for ISP restoration
body: The internet provider has reported an outage.
Monitor its service status and wait for restoration.
Contact the ISP if you need an estimated restoration time.

checkFibreConnection.title: Is the router connected to a separate fibre ONT?
body: Look at the router's WAN or Internet port.
Check whether an Ethernet cable runs from that port to a separate fibre box (ONT), usually mounted on a wall.
If it is connected to an ONT, select Fibre ONT.
If the router uses a SIM card or another type of broadband connection, select No ONT.
If unsure, follow the cable from the router's WAN port or check the router's connection settings.
Some routers have 4G/5G backup, so check which connection is currently active if both are available.

checkMobileBroadband.title: Does the router use 4G or 5G mobile broadband?
body: Check whether the router contains a SIM card and connects to the mobile network.
Look for LTE, 4G, 5G, Cellular or Mobile Network on its display or administration page.
You can usually find the router's administration address using the Default Gateway shown by ipconfig on a connected Windows computer.
A router may provide strong Wi-Fi even when its mobile internet connection has a weak signal.
If the connection uses mobile broadband, continue with the mobile network checks.
For DSL, cable or another connection type, follow the general modem checks.

link.name: One NZ wireless broadband modem setup
link.description: Examples of SIM-based broadband modems and cellular connection indicators.

checkMobileBroadband.caption: An example mobile broadband modem. Models and signal indicators vary between providers.

checkMobileSignal.title: Check mobile broadband signal strength
body: Look at the mobile signal indicator on the router or its administration page.
Check whether the router has registered on a 4G or 5G network.
Poor signal, missing network registration or repeated disconnections can prevent internet access.
Remember that the Wi-Fi signal shown on your computer only measures the connection to the router, not the router's mobile connection.
Check whether the cellular signal is weak or unavailable.

link.name: One NZ wireless broadband signal indicators
link.description: Official examples of mobile modem signal lights and what their colours mean.

improveMobileReception.title: Improve mobile broadband reception
body: Move the mobile broadband router closer to a window, ideally higher up and away from obstructions.
Avoid placing it inside cupboards, behind televisions or near large metal objects.
Try different windows or rooms and allow the router to reconnect after each move.
Check the cellular signal indicator or router status page after each change.
Keep the router within any placement restrictions required by the provider.
When signal improves, test internet access again.

link.name: 2degrees modem placement advice
link.description: Official advice on positioning 4G and 5G broadband modems for better reception.

checkMobileRegistration.title: Check mobile network registration and SIM status
body: Open the router's administration page or manufacturer's app if available.
Check whether the SIM is recognised and the router is registered with the mobile network.
Look for messages such as No SIM, SIM Error, Not Registered or No Service.
If the provider supplies the SIM and router, avoid changing APN or authentication settings without checking its instructions.
If the SIM is not recognised, follow the manufacturer's instructions for checking it while the router is powered off.
If registration is normal, continue testing the mobile connection.

testMobileConnection.title: Test the mobile broadband connection
body: Check whether the router has obtained a mobile data connection and internet access.
Try opening several websites from a connected computer or phone.
If the connection works intermittently or becomes very slow at certain times, tower congestion or changing reception may be contributing.
Compare results at different times or router positions if practical.
If the router is registered but internet access still fails, contact the provider for service and SIM checks.

contactMobileIsp.title: Contact the mobile broadband provider
body: Mobile broadband is still not working after checking signal, router placement and network registration.
Record the router model, 4G/5G signal status, SIM status and any error messages.
Ask the provider to check the SIM activation, mobile network service, local tower issues and account status.
Do not factory-reset the router or change APN settings unless the provider recommends it.

link.name: One NZ wireless broadband troubleshooting
link.description: Example provider instructions for mobile broadband equipment and signal issues.

powerOffOnt.title: Power down the fibre ONT
body: This is an extended power-reset procedure after ordinary troubleshooting has failed.
Switch off the router and disconnect power to the ONT using its power switch or power supply.
Do not press the recessed factory Reset button or disconnect the fibre-optic cable.
Leave the ONT powered off for approximately ten minutes.
While the ONT is off, review the router's WAN configuration if the router is accessible.
Internet-based telephone services and other connections may be unavailable while the equipment is off.
The ten-minute interval is an additional troubleshooting attempt, not a requirement for every ONT or ISP.

link.name: Chorus ONT-500 equipment guide
link.description: Official illustrations showing ONT power controls and the separate Reset button.

powerOffOnt.alt: Chorus fibre ONT power switch and reset button
powerOffOnt.caption: Use the power control, not the recessed factory Reset button. Other ONTs may look different.

checkWanSettings.title: Check router WAN settings
body: Open the router administration page if accessible.
Locate Internet, WAN or Ethernet WAN settings.
Check that the connection type matches the ISP requirements, such as DHCP/IPoE or PPPoE.
Check whether VLAN tagging is required and verify the VLAN ID and priority.
For example, 2degrees fibre specifies DHCP, VLAN ID 10 and priority 0.
These settings are ISP-specific and must not be assumed for every connection.
If the settings already match the provider's requirements, leave them unchanged.

link.name: 2degrees BYO router configuration
link.description: Official fibre WAN settings showing an example of DHCP, VLAN ID 10 and priority 0.

correctWanSettings.title: Confirm and correct WAN configuration
body: Find the WAN configuration required by the customer's actual internet provider.
Check the connection protocol, login details where required, VLAN tagging, VLAN ID and priority.
Record the original values before making any changes.
Only correct values you have confirmed are wrong.
If the required settings are unknown, do not guess. Leave the configuration unchanged and continue to restore the connection.

link.name: Example ISP WAN requirements
link.description: 2degrees settings illustrate the information to confirm with the customer's own provider.

restoreOnt.title: Restore ONT and router power
body: After approximately ten minutes, switch the ONT back on.
Allow its optical connection indicators to stabilise.
Turn the router back on and wait for the WAN connection to establish.
Check the router's internet status and test several websites.
If the ONT indicates an optical fault, contact the provider rather than repeatedly resetting it.

checkDirectConnection.title: Check the modem or router connection
body: For fibre, inspect the Ethernet connection between the ONT and the router WAN port.
For DSL or other services, check the appropriate modem and incoming connection.
Try another suitable cable where possible.
If the provider supports it, test with a compatible replacement router or an approved direct connection method.
A computer connected directly to a fibre ONT may require VLAN tagging or authentication settings before internet access works.
A failed direct test alone does not prove that the ISP connection is faulty.

link.name: One NZ fibre modem installation
link.description: Illustrations showing an ONT connected to a router's WAN port.

checkDirectConnection.alt: Ethernet cable connecting an ONT to a router WAN port
checkDirectConnection.caption: Example fibre ONT-to-router connection. Port positions vary by model.

routerFaultLikely.title: Router fault or configuration issue likely
body: Internet access works using an alternative router or ISP-supported direct connection.
This suggests the original router, its WAN settings or its cabling may be responsible.
Review the router configuration before replacing hardware.

contactIsp.title: Contact ISP
body: Local troubleshooting has not restored internet access.
Record the equipment status lights and any error messages.
Tell the provider whether multiple devices are affected.
Report any router restart, ONT reset, WAN configuration checks and cable tests completed.
Ask the ISP to check the service and confirm its required connection settings.
Avoid factory-resetting network equipment unless instructed to do so.
